review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner (self-review, not independent approval)
review.decision: Implement the known-session identity fix and regression tests
review.notes: Reproduced an attached Ghostty tab being missed because the real tmux session starts with punctuation. Preserve the requested name byte-for-byte, try literal identity before skipping leading decoration, and prefer a literal tab over a decorated lookalike. Keep the existing strict session/window separator and exact raw AppleScript title including trailing spaces. Do not rename live sessions, change restore parsing, expand terminal permissions, or send agent input. Synthetic pure tests cover matching/selection; a bounded live focus of the user-requested pane separately checks Ghostty integration. No claim of native menu-click or other-terminal UI acceptance from pure tests.

cases.description: Known-session matching preserves legal leading punctuation and Unicode while tolerating terminal alert decoration
cases.setup: Synthetic bare/windowed titles with curly or ASCII quotes, dashes, emoji and symbol-only names; repeated alert markers and whitespace; unrelated or prefix-sharing names.
cases.action: Call the shared TitleMatchesSession matcher with the complete unchanged session identity for positive and negative tables.
cases.expected: Literal and decorated versions of the complete session match; differently quoted, truncated, unrelated, wrong-separator and empty identities do not. Existing ordinary/decorated titles and bare trailing-whitespace tolerance remain supported.
surfaces: Shared terminal title matching and notification visibility

cases.description: Ghostty tab selection prefers literal identity and preserves the exact raw title used to focus
cases.setup: Ordered synthetic tab records with an earlier decorated lookalike, a later literal match, quoted session identities and raw titles ending in spaces/tabs; empty or unrelated lists.
cases.action: Resolve the requested session through the same pure tab-selection helper used by FocusTab.
cases.expected: A literal match wins across all tabs before tolerant decoration fallback. With only a decorated match it is selected. The chosen record, indices and trailing title bytes remain unchanged; no match and empty session return false. Multiple literal tabs retain first-match order.
